claims.text: WTaTiVZr has improved plastic strain relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
WTaTiVZr has improved toughness relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The improved plastic strain and toughness are governed by alloy-induced microstructural refinement.
Multi-element additions produce significant lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr.
The alloy possesses a fine, nanostructured grain-boundary network.
The nanostructured grain-boundary network facilitates distributed dislocation activity.
The nanostructured grain-boundary network delays crack initiation.
Lattice distortions generated by the multi-element composition drive grain-boundary refinement.
The proposed refined microstructure lowers the threshold for dislocation nucleation.
The proposed microstructure promotes grain-boundary sliding.
The proposed microstructure retards crack initiation and propagation.
Under identical high-temperature tests, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature tests, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The proposed effect is expected to hold from approximately 900°C to 1400°C.
Outside 900°C to 1400°C, or under extreme irradiation, additional failure mechanisms may limit the proposed effect.
Matching grain size and processing history between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten is proposed as a controlled comparison.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement in both plastic strain and fracture toughness would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a refined grain-boundary network and associated lattice distortions would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The materials are to have comparable grain sizes and microstructural states, while the claimed causal distinction is an alloy-specific refined, nanostructured grain-boundary network. Matching away the proposed refinement prevents the comparison from directly testing whether that refinement causes the performance difference.
